## Terminal fonts

- Font fields are now a drop-down of your installed monospaced fonts, each shown in its own typeface. You can still type a name, for a fallback list or a font that isn't installed.
- Terminal fonts that don't mark themselves as monospaced, such as Geist Mono, are recognized too. Fonts installed while resesh is running show up without a restart.
- Settings splits the font setting into Terminal font and Fallback fonts (for example a Nerd Font for icons), with a Reset. Picking a font no longer drops your fallbacks.
- A session's font goes in front of the app's fonts instead of replacing them. Choose "Use app setting" to clear it.

## Editors

- The local profile editor has tabs like the session editor: Shell, Appearance and Notes. Notes for local profiles can now be edited, and errors show under the field they're about.
- The session editor no longer scrolls. Icon, color and appearance overrides move to a new Appearance tab, and both editors fit short windows without cutting off the last fields.
- Fixed several arguments or environment lines in a local profile saving as one line.

## Title bar

- The New SSH session button is gone from the title bar; use the File menu or the sessions pane. New Telnet session is now in both menus.
- Quick connect stays a full search box on narrower windows.

Choose the x64 download for Intel or AMD PCs. Choose ARM64 only for Windows on ARM devices.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/bpbp-boop/resesh/compare/v0.22.0...v0.23.0)
